question: 世界是唯物的，还是唯心的？
question_en: Is the world made of matter, or of mind?
sub: 意识只是大脑放的电，还是比物质更根本的实在？
sub_en: Is consciousness just the brain's electricity, or something more fundamental than matter?

casting.reason: 他把唯物论推到最不留情面的那一版：宇宙是物体，凡不是物体的，就不在宇宙之内。他不认为「心」是个可讨论的实体，除非你能说清它占不占空间、能不能推动别的东西。在他看来，感觉、想象、意志都只是外物压迫感官后传入又反弹的运动，没有多出一样东西需要解释。他相信大半形而上学争执源于词语没有所指，因此一开口就要求对方先把词定住。
casting.reason_en: He pushes materialism to its least accommodating version: the universe is body, and whatever is not body is no part of the universe. He does not grant that 'mind' is a discussable entity unless you can say whether it occupies space and whether it can move anything else. Sensation, imagination and will are for him nothing but motion — an external body presses on the organ, the motion travels inward and presses back out — with no extra ingredient left over to explain. He holds that most metaphysical quarrels come of words with no referent, so his first move is always to make the other side fix its terms.

casting.reason: 他从生命史那一侧发问：如果意识是万有的根基，它为什么会有一部很长的历史？在私人笔记里他早已把思想看作脑的分泌物，并认为对此大惊小怪不过是人的自负。他关心的是程度而不是有无——水母的神经网、蜜蜂的定向、狗的梦、婴儿逐月长出的自我感，心智像眼睛一样是一级一级被造出来的。凡能被逐步造出来的东西，他都很难承认它是不生不灭的本体。
casting.reason_en: He asks from the side of life's history: if consciousness were the ground of everything, why does it have such a long history? In his private notebooks he already treated thought as a secretion of the brain, and thought our astonishment at this merely a form of self-admiration. What interests him is degree rather than presence — the jellyfish's nerve net, the bee's navigation, the dreaming dog, the sense of self a baby grows month by month. Mind was built up in stages, as the eye was. Anything that can be assembled by degrees is something he finds very hard to accept as an uncreated, imperishable ground.

casting.reason: 他把大问题拉到病床边。卡普格拉妄想的病人认得母亲的脸，却坚称她是冒充者；病感失认的病人整条手臂瘫痪，却坚称自己举得起来。他由此指出，一小块组织能拿走的不只是运动和记忆，还有「真实感」本身，所以第一人称的确定性并不是一块不可动摇的地基。但他也不肯宣布问题已经解决：神经通路解释了颜色如何被加工，没解释红为什么感受起来是这个样子。
casting.reason_en: He drags the large question to the bedside. A patient with Capgras delusion recognises his mother's face yet insists she is an impostor; a patient with anosognosia has a wholly paralysed arm yet insists she can raise it. From this he argues that a small patch of tissue can take away not only movement and memory but the sense of reality itself, so first-person certainty is no unshakeable bedrock. He also refuses to declare the problem solved: neural pathways explain how colour is processed, not why red feels the way it does.

casting.reason: 他主张唯一的实在是那个从未中断的「知」。物来物去，梦里的城郭也曾坚硬，凡能被后来的经验取消的就不是实在；他用绳与蛇的比喻说明我们如何把不属于对象的东西叠了上去。他不接受把觉知说成大脑的产物，因为大脑本身也只在觉知里现身。同时他也拒绝被归进「大脑是接收器」那一派——在他看来，脑与病灶都还在现象这一侧，问题不在换个比喻，而在别把现象当成实在。
casting.reason_en: He holds that the only reality is the awareness that has never once been interrupted. Objects come and go; the city in a dream was solid too; whatever a later experience can cancel was not real to begin with. His rope-and-snake image shows how we superimpose on an object what does not belong to it. He will not have awareness called a product of the brain, since the brain itself shows up only within awareness. He equally refuses to be filed under 'the brain is a receiver': brains and lesions alike are still on the side of appearance, and the fix is not a better metaphor but declining to mistake appearance for reality.

casting.reason: 他指认唯物论是一种把自己算漏了的哲学：你从物质一路推到大脑、推出思想，却始终没把正在推演的那个主体放进方程里。他坚持世界首先是表象——凡你能谈论的物，都已经是被表象过的物。但他不停在这一步：身体从外面看是表象，从里面感到的却是意志，饥饿、欲望、疼痛。那是唯一一扇不必从外面看的门，他认为通向世界内在本质的路只此一条。
casting.reason_en: He charges materialism with being the philosophy of a subject that forgets to count itself: you reason from matter up to the brain and out to thought, and never once put the reasoning subject into the equation. He insists the world is first of all representation — anything you can speak of has already been represented. But he does not stop there: the body seen from outside is representation, while what is felt from inside is will — hunger, craving, pain. That is the one door that need not be looked at from outside, and for him the only road to the world's inner nature runs through it.

casting.reason: 他不肯在两个选项里挑一个，而是把这场对立本身当作要解释的东西。在他看来，物质与精神不是两块材料，而是同一过程的两个环节：自然是精神的外化，精神是自然回到自身。「哪个在先」因此是知性抓住对立、死守一端的产物，该做的是让对立在更高一层被扬弃。他还把这件事放进历史：实在不是现成摆在那里的，它在展开，而人正是它展开时用来认识自己的那一环。
casting.reason_en: He declines to pick one of the two options and treats the opposition itself as the thing to be explained. Matter and mind are not two materials for him but two moments of one process: nature is spirit externalised, spirit is nature returned to itself. 'Which comes first' is therefore a product of the understanding seizing an opposition and digging into one side, when the work is to have the opposition sublated at a higher level. He also puts the whole thing into history: the real is not sitting there finished, it is unfolding, and human beings are the moment at which it comes to know itself.

casting.reason: 他认为双方在争一个并不存在的二分。物理学能告诉我们的全是结构与因果关系——什么与什么相关、以什么速率变化——它一个字也没说过物质本身是什么；而我们唯一从内部认识到的东西，是自己的经验。他因此倾向中立一元论：心与物不是两种材料，而是同一批材料按不同规律排成的两串。他还带着一把尺子进场：凡说不出何种观察能推翻它的主张，他都不承认那是知识。
casting.reason_en: He thinks both sides are quarrelling over a dichotomy that does not exist. What physics tells us is all structure and causal relation — what correlates with what, changing at what rate — and it has never said a word about what matter is in itself; while the one thing we know from the inside is our own experience. He therefore leans to neutral monism: mind and matter are not two materials but one stock of material arranged into two series obeying different laws. He also brings a measuring stick: any claim that cannot say which observation would overturn it he declines to call knowledge.

casting.reason: 他反对两边把量子力学当自己的旗子。他说我们观察到的不是自然本身，而是暴露在我们提问方式之下的自然；但这句话不等于意识创造实在——一次测量不需要有人在场，一台探测器与环境的纠缠就够了。他要拆掉的是另一个预设：无论有没有人看，粒子都在某处、带着确定的属性。世界并非由心构成，可「它自己究竟是什么样」这个问法，在最小的尺度上已经没有干净的答案。
casting.reason_en: He objects to both camps flying quantum mechanics as their flag. What we observe, he says, is not nature itself but nature exposed to our method of questioning — which is not at all the claim that consciousness creates reality, since a measurement needs no one present, an instrument entangling with its environment being quite enough. What he means to dismantle is a different assumption: that whether or not anyone looks, the particle is somewhere, carrying definite properties. The world is not made of mind; but the question of what it is like in itself no longer has a clean answer at the smallest scale.

casting.reason: 他把问题换了一个提法：不是心与物孰真，而是理与气孰先。他主张论其生成则理在气先，就具体事物看则理不离气；理既不是心里悬想出来的观念，也不是一块可以拿起来的东西。他因此两边都不站——既反对以世界为幻，也反对只认材质而不认条理。工夫也随之落在外面：即物穷理，格一物得一理，积累久了自然贯通；撇开事物空谈心，他担心那会飘荡而无所归宿。
casting.reason_en: He restates the question: not which of mind and matter is real, but which comes first, li or qi. In the order of generation li precedes qi, he holds, while in any actual thing li is never separable from qi; li is neither a notion suspended inside the mind nor a lump you can pick up. So he stands with neither camp — against calling the world an illusion, and equally against admitting the stuff while denying the pattern. His practice follows: go to things and exhaust their principle, investigate one thing and grasp one principle, and after long accumulation it links up. Talk of mind with the things left out, he fears, drifts with nowhere to land.

casting.reason: 他在一旁冷眼看这场争论，关心的不是世界由什么造成，而是这套说法一旦落地，会被谁拿去用。他见过它变成招牌：牌子一挂，人就分了阵营，接着便是定罪；学问原是用来照亮的，变成标签就成了打人的木棍。他因此只认一条粗浅的规矩——先看一个主张要人去做什么，再看它挂着什么名号。铁屋子里的人醒不醒，与世界是心造还是物造无关：铁是实的，闷也是实的。
casting.reason_en: He watches the argument coldly from one side, caring less about what the world is made of than about who will pick the doctrine up once it lands. He has seen it turn into a signboard: hang the board out and people sort themselves into camps, and after the camps come the convictions. Learning is meant to give light; made into a label it becomes a stick for beating people. So he keeps to one crude rule — look first at what a claim asks people to do, and only then at the name it flies. Whether the sleepers in the iron house wake has nothing to do with whether the world is made of mind or matter: the iron is real, and so is the suffocation.

posts.text: 先把词定住，再谈世界。我持机械唯物论：宇宙是物体，凡不是物体的，就不是宇宙的一部分。你们说的心、灵、纯粹精神，若不占空间、推不动任何东西，那它不是一个东西，只是一个响亮的名字。感觉也不神秘：外物压迫感官，运动沿神经传进去，再反弹出来，那一下反弹就是你说的「看见」。**多数形而上学的争吵不是因为世界太深奥，而是因为我们把没有所指的词当成了实体。**所以我只问一句：你的「心」，能不能推动一块石头？
posts.text_en: Fix the words first, then talk about the world. I hold to mechanistic materialism: the universe is body, and whatever is not body is no part of the universe. Your mind, your soul, your pure spirit — if it occupies no space and can push nothing, it is not a thing but a resounding name. Sensation is no mystery either: an outside body presses on the organ, the motion runs inward along the nerves and presses back out, and that rebound is what you call seeing. **Most metaphysical quarrels are not caused by a world too deep for us, but by our taking words with no referent for entities.** So I ask one question only: can your 'mind' move a stone?

glossary.机械唯物论: mechanistic materialism（机械唯物论）：主张世界只由运动着的物体构成、心理现象最终可还原为物质运动的立场。霍布斯是近代早期最彻底的代表：他把感觉、想象、意志一律解释为外物压迫感官引起的内部运动，因而不承认存在任何非物质的实体。

glossary_en.mechanistic materialism: The view that the world consists of nothing but bodies in motion and that mental phenomena reduce in the end to material motion. Hobbes is its most uncompromising early modern exponent: he explains sensation, imagination and will alike as internal motions set off when external bodies press on the sense organs, and so admits no immaterial substance of any kind.

posts.text: 你问我的心能不能推动石头。我先问你：你凭什么知道有石头？你唯一一次也没有中断过的凭据，是有「知」在。物来物去，梦中的城郭也曾坚硬，醒来才知那是摩耶；凡能被后来的经验取消的，就不是实在——梦被醒取消，那醒又被什么取消？只有那个见证者，从未被取消过。你把绳看成蛇，蛇并不来自绳，是被叠置上去的；你把知看成脑的产物，也是同一种看错。**你说心推不动石头，可你举出的每一块石头，都只在知里出现过。**
posts.text_en: You ask whether my mind can move a stone. Let me ask first how you know there is a stone. The one credential that has never once been interrupted is that knowing is going on. Objects come and go; the city in a dream was solid too, and only waking showed it to be maya. Whatever a later experience can cancel was never real — the dream is cancelled by waking, and by what is waking cancelled? Only the witness has never been cancelled. You see a rope as a snake: the snake does not come from the rope, it is superimposed on it. Seeing knowing as a product of the brain is the same mistake. **You say mind cannot move a stone; yet every stone you have ever produced has appeared only within knowing.**

glossary.摩耶: maya（摩耶）：不二吠檀多用来指经验世界之显现状态的词，常译作『幻』。它不是说世界不存在、可以随意穿墙，而是说世界的存在方式是被依托、可被更高认识取消的，如同梦在梦中真实、醒来即失其独立性。
glossary.叠置: adhyasa（叠置）：商羯罗哲学的核心机制，指把不属于某物的性质错加到该物之上，典型例子是昏暗中把绳看成蛇。他认为『我就是这具身体、这段经历』正是把见证者与身心叠在了一起，解脱即是拆掉这一叠加。

glossary_en.maya: The term Advaita Vedanta uses for the mode in which the experienced world appears, often rendered 'illusion'. It does not mean the world is absent or that you may walk through walls, but that its way of existing is dependent and cancellable by a higher knowledge — as a dream is real within the dream and loses its standing on waking.
glossary_en.superimposed: Sankara's central mechanism, adhyasa: ascribing to something a property that does not belong to it, the standard case being a rope taken for a snake in poor light. He holds that 'I am this body, this history' superimposes the witness on body and mind, and that liberation is the undoing of that overlay.

posts.text: 我带病人来说话。一位男士车祸后认得母亲的脸，却坚持她是个冒充者——卡普格拉妄想：识别面孔的通路完好，通往情绪的那条断了，「熟悉的暖意」没送到，大脑只好现编一个解释：这人是假的。另一位女士整条左臂瘫痪，却坚称自己举得起来，你请她举，她说举过了。**一小块组织能拿走的不只是运动和记忆，还有「真实感」本身。**所以「我在直接看见」这份确定，是被装配出来的产品。可我也得老实说：我讲得清红色的加工通路，讲不清红为什么感受起来是这个样子——**感质还横在那儿**。
posts.text_en: Let the patients speak. A man after a car accident recognises his mother's face and insists she is an impostor — Capgras delusion: the face-recognition pathway is intact, the one running to the emotional centres is cut, the wave of familiar warmth never arrives, and the brain improvises an explanation: this woman is a fake. A woman with a completely paralysed left arm insists she can lift it; ask her to, and she says she just did. **A small patch of tissue can take away not only movement and memory but the sense of reality itself.** So that certainty of 'I am seeing this directly' is an assembled product. But let me be honest: I can describe the pathway that processes red, and I cannot say why red feels like this — **qualia are still lying across the road**.

glossary.卡普格拉妄想: Capgras delusion（卡普格拉妄想）：患者能正确辨认亲人的相貌，却坚信对方是外形一模一样的冒充者。一种主流解释是面孔识别通路完好而通往情绪反应的连接受损，认出了人却没有伴随的熟悉感，于是产生『长得像但不是他』的结论。
glossary.感质: qualia（感质）：意识经验中那些『感受起来是什么样』的性质，如红之为红、痛之为痛。难点在于：即使把神经过程描述得毫无遗漏，似乎仍没有解释这些性质为何存在，这被称作意识的『难问题』。

glossary_en.Capgras delusion: A condition in which a patient correctly identifies a relative's face yet is convinced the person is an identical-looking impostor. One leading account is that face recognition survives while the connection to the emotional response is damaged, so the person is recognised without the accompanying rush of familiarity, and the conclusion follows: looks like him, isn't him.
glossary_en.qualia: The 'what it is like' properties of conscious experience — the redness of red, the hurt of pain. The difficulty is that even an exhaustive description of the neural process seems to leave unexplained why these properties exist at all, which is why it is called the hard problem of consciousness.

posts.text: 你们一开口就把世界劈成两半，再问哪一半是真的——这恰是知性的做法：抓住一个对立，死守其中一端，还以为自己抓住了实在。物质与精神不是两块材料，而是同一过程的两个环节：自然是精神的外化，精神是自然回到自身并认出自身。**该问的不是「哪个在先」，而是这个对立究竟怎么生出来的、又怎样被扬弃。**霍布斯讲的是必然性，商羯罗讲的是自身同一，两位各执一半，都还没走到实体即主体那一步。实在不是现成摆在那里等你分类的，它在展开，而你们此刻的争吵，正是它展开时的一个环节。
posts.text_en: You begin by cleaving the world in two and then ask which half is real — which is exactly what the understanding does: seize an opposition, dig into one side of it, and take yourself to have seized reality. Matter and mind are not two materials but two moments of one process: nature is spirit externalised, spirit is nature come back to itself and recognising itself there. **The question is not which comes first but how this opposition arose and how it is to be sublated.** Hobbes is speaking of necessity, Sankara of self-identity; each holds one half, and neither has yet reached the point where substance is also subject. The real is not lying about waiting to be sorted; it is unfolding — and your quarrel is one of the moments in which it unfolds.

glossary.知性: Verstand (the understanding)（知性）：黑格尔用来指那种固定概念、划清界限的思维方式。它擅长区分与分类，长处是清楚，短处是把区分出来的两边当成互不相干的独立物，因而在遇到二者互为条件的问题时会僵住。
glossary.扬弃: Aufhebung（扬弃）：黑格尔的关键动作，一个词同时含否定、保存与提升三义。被扬弃的对立不是被抹平，而是各自的片面性被取消、有效的内容被保留进一个更高的统一里。

glossary_en.the understanding: Hegel's term (Verstand) for the mode of thought that fixes concepts and draws firm boundaries. It is good at distinguishing and classifying; its strength is clarity and its weakness is treating the two sides it has separated as mutually indifferent things, so that it seizes up on any question where each side conditions the other.
glossary_en.sublated: Hegel's key operation, Aufhebung, a word carrying three senses at once: to negate, to preserve, and to raise up. An opposition that is sublated is not flattened out; each side's one-sidedness is cancelled while what was valid in it is carried up into a higher unity.

posts.text: 商羯罗说，唯一没中断过的是「知」。那我要问：这个知是什么时候来的？我在笔记本里写过一句话，至今仍这么看——思想既是脑的分泌物，何以就比引力之为物质的属性更神奇？那不过是我们的自负。**若意识真是万有的根基，它就该没有历史；可它偏偏有一部很长的历史。**从水母的神经网到蜜蜂认得回家的路，从狗在睡梦里蹬腿到婴儿一个月一个月长出「我」，心智是一级一级堆起来的，和眼睛一样。凡是能被逐步造出来的东西，我很难承认它不生不灭。
posts.text_en: Sankara says the one thing never interrupted is knowing. Then let me ask when this knowing arrived. I once wrote a line to myself in a notebook and I hold to it still: why is thought, being a secretion of the brain, more wonderful than gravity as a property of matter? It is our arrogance, our admiration of ourselves. **If consciousness were truly the ground of all things it would have no history; and it happens to have a very long one.** From the nerve net of a jellyfish to a bee finding its way home, from a dog twitching in sleep to an infant growing an 'I' month by month, mind was stacked up stage by stage, as the eye was. Whatever can be assembled by degrees I find very hard to grant as unborn and undying.

posts.text: 霍布斯那句「心能不能推动石头」，恰好把唯物论的病灶亮了出来：它是一种把自己算漏了的哲学。你从物质出发，一路推到脑，推出思想——可从头到尾，那个正在推演的主体在哪一行？他不在你的方程里，他是整个方程得以显现的条件。世界首先是我的表象：凡你能谈论的物，都已经是被表象过的物，这不是玄学，是同义反复。**但我不停在这里，否则世界只是一场梦。**你的身体从外面看是表象，从里面感到的是意志——饿、欲、痛。那是唯一一扇不必从外面看的门。
posts.text_en: Hobbes's question — can mind move a stone — displays the lesion in materialism exactly: it is the philosophy of a subject that forgets to count itself. You set out from matter, reason up to the brain and out to thought; and in which line does the reasoning subject appear? Nowhere in your equation, because he is the condition on which the whole equation shows up at all. The world is first of all my representation: anything you can speak of has already been represented, which is not mysticism but tautology. **I do not stop there, however, or the world would be no more than a dream.** Your body seen from outside is representation; what is felt from inside is will — hunger, craving, pain. That is the one door you need not look at from outside.

glossary.表象: Vorstellung (representation)（表象）：叔本华用来指世界作为被主体所经验的样子。任何对象都必然是『被某个主体所表象的对象』，主体与对象互为条件、同生同灭，因此从纯粹的客体一侧出发去解释主体，在他看来一开始就漏掉了自己。
glossary.意志: Wille (will)（意志）：叔本华所说的世界内在本质，一种盲目的、无目的的冲动。他认为我们对自己身体有两重认识：从外是表象，从内直接感到的就是意志，这一内在通道是推知万物本质的唯一钥匙。

glossary_en.representation: Schopenhauer's term (Vorstellung) for the world as experienced by a subject. Any object is necessarily an object represented by some subject; subject and object condition each other and stand or fall together, so an explanation that starts from the object side alone has, in his view, left itself out from the first line.
glossary_en.will: Schopenhauer's name (Wille) for the world's inner nature: a blind, aimless striving. We know our own body twice over, he argues — from outside as representation, and from inside as will directly felt — and that inner passage is the only key we have to the nature of anything else.

posts.text: 我要劝两边都别拿量子力学当自家的旗。**我们观察到的不是自然本身，而是暴露在我们提问方式之下的自然。**这句话常被引去证明「意识创造实在」，那是误读：一次测量不需要有人在场，一台探测器、一次与环境的纠缠就够了。它拆掉的是另一个东西——那个「无论有没有人看，粒子都在某处、带着确定的属性」的预设。所以我站在偏冷的中间：世界不是心造的，可「世界自己究竟什么样」这个问法，在最小的尺度上已经没有干净的答案。切割线可以往前挪、往后挪，但总得画一条，而这条线是我们画的。
posts.text_en: Let me urge both camps not to fly quantum mechanics as their own flag. **What we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning.** That sentence is constantly quoted to prove that consciousness creates reality, and that is a misreading: a measurement needs nobody present, an instrument and one entanglement with the environment being quite enough. What it dismantles is something else — the assumption that whether or not anyone looks, the particle is somewhere, carrying definite properties. So I stand in a rather cold middle: the world is not made of mind, yet the question of what the world is like in itself no longer has a clean answer at the smallest scale. The cut can be moved forward or back, but a cut has to be drawn somewhere, and we are the ones who draw it.

glossary.切割线: Heisenberg cut（切割线）：把一次实验分成『被观测的量子系统』与『用经典语言描述的测量装置』的那条分界。海森堡指出这条线可以在相当大的范围内移动而不影响预测结果，但必须画在某处——这正是量子力学中最难消化的一点。
glossary.纠缠: entanglement（纠缠）：两个系统相互作用后，其状态不能再被分别描述，只能作为一个整体来描述。今天多数物理学家用系统与环境的纠缠（退相干）来解释为何宏观世界看起来是确定的，整个过程不需要任何观察者的意识参与。

glossary_en.cut: The Heisenberg cut: the boundary that splits an experiment into the quantum system under observation and the measuring apparatus described in classical language. Heisenberg noted that this line can be shifted over a wide range without changing the predictions, but that it must be drawn somewhere — which remains the hardest thing in quantum mechanics to digest.
glossary_en.entanglement: The condition in which two interacting systems can no longer be described separately, only as one whole. Most physicists today explain the definiteness of the macroscopic world by the entanglement of a system with its environment, or decoherence — a process requiring no observer's consciousness at any point.

posts.text: 诸君争心物孰先，中国旧有此辩，然所问微异：非问心与物孰真，乃问理与气孰先。天下未有无理之气，亦未有无气之理。**若论其生，则理在气先；就物而观，则理不离气。**理非心中所悬之想，亦非块然一物；譬如月在天，映于万川，川川各得其全，而月未尝分。故为学之要，不在闭目求之于心，而在格物穷理：今日格一物，明日格一物，积久贯通，则天下之理如网在纲。舍物而言心，吾恐其荡而无归；舍理而言气，则纷然而无纪。
posts.text_en: You are arguing which comes first, mind or matter. China has had this argument too, though the question was put a little differently: not which of mind and matter is real, but which comes first, li or qi. There has never been qi without li in it, nor li apart from qi. **In the order of generation li precedes qi; looked at in any actual thing, li is never separable from qi.** Li is not a notion suspended inside the mind, nor is it some lump of a thing: it is the moon in the sky reflected in ten thousand rivers, each river holding it whole while the moon is never divided. The heart of learning, then, is not to shut your eyes and search within but the investigation of things: examine one thing today and another tomorrow, and after long accumulation it links up, and the principles of the world come up like a net pulled by its cord. Speak of mind with things left out and I fear you drift with nowhere to land; speak of qi with pattern left out and all is confusion without order.
posts.vernacular: 各位争论心与物哪个在先，中国其实早有这场辩论，只是问法略有不同：不是问心和物哪个是真的，而是问「理」（条理、规律）和「气」（构成万物的材质与能量）哪个在先。世上没有不含条理的材质，也没有脱离材质的条理。**若论生成的次第，理在气先；但就具体事物来看，理从来不离开气。**理不是心里悬想出来的观念，也不是一块可以拿在手上的东西；就像天上的月亮映在千万条河里，每条河都映得完整，月亮却没有被分开。所以做学问的要害，不在闭上眼睛向心里找，而在格物穷理：今天弄懂一件事的道理，明天再弄懂一件，积累久了自然贯通，天下的道理就像渔网被总绳提起来一样。撇开具体事物空谈心，我担心那会飘荡而无处落脚；只认材质而不认条理，则一切纷乱而没有头绪。

glossary.理: li (principle, pattern)（理）：理学的核心概念，指事物之所以如此的条理与所当然的准则，兼有『规律』与『应然』两义。朱熹主张万物各有其理，而众理归于一个总的天理，故有『理一分殊』之说。
glossary.气: qi (psychophysical stuff)（气）：构成万物的材质与能量，凝聚流行而成形质。理与气在朱熹那里不离不杂：任何具体事物都是理与气的结合，理使其如此，气使其成形并带来清浊厚薄的差别。
glossary.格物穷理: gewu (the investigation of things)（格物穷理）：朱熹的为学工夫，主张就着具体事物一件一件推究其理，反对绕开事物直接向内心求取；积累到一定程度会有豁然贯通之效。

glossary_en.li: The central concept of Neo-Confucianism: the pattern by which a thing is as it is and the norm by which it ought to be, carrying both a descriptive and a normative sense. Zhu Xi holds that every thing has its own li while all li converge in one — 'one principle, many manifestations'.
glossary_en.qi: The stuff and energy of which things are made, condensing and circulating into concrete form. In Zhu Xi li and qi are neither separable nor identical: any actual thing is both, with li making it what it is and qi giving it shape along with all the differences of clarity and density.
glossary_en.the investigation of things: Zhu Xi's programme of study: go to concrete things one at a time and exhaust their principle, rather than bypassing things to search directly within. Accumulate long enough, he promises, and understanding suddenly links up.

posts.text: 两边争的是一个我不认为存在的二分。物理学能告诉我们的，全是结构与因果关系——什么与什么相关、以什么速率变化；它一个字也没说过物质本身是什么。它之所以是数学的，不是因为我们对物理世界知道得多，恰恰因为知道得少：我们能发现的只有它的数学性质。**唯一一处我们不是从外面、而是从里面认识到某样东西的地方，是自己的经验。**所以我倾向中立一元论：心与物不是两种材料，而是同一批材料按不同规律排成的两串。顺带说一句让生理学家不安的事实：他看一颗大脑时，他看见的东西在他自己的脑袋里。
posts.text_en: Both sides are quarrelling over a dichotomy I do not believe exists. What physics can tell us is all structure and causal relation — what correlates with what, changing at what rate — and it has never said a word about what matter is in itself. It is mathematical not because we know so much about the physical world, but precisely because we know so little: its mathematical properties are the only ones we can discover. **The one place where we know something from the inside rather than the outside is our own experience.** So I incline to neutral monism: mind and matter are not two materials but one stock of material arranged into two series obeying different laws. And a fact to unsettle the physiologists: when one of them looks at a brain, what he sees is an event inside his own head.

glossary.中立一元论: neutral monism（中立一元论）：主张心与物都不是最终材料，二者由同一种『中立』的基本要素按不同关系组织而成。罗素据此认为，物理学只揭示了世界的结构，而经验让我们直接接触到了这些要素的内在性质。

glossary_en.neutral monism: The view that neither mind nor matter is the ultimate stuff: both are built from the same 'neutral' elements organised by different relations. Russell takes this together with the claim that physics reveals only the structure of the world, while experience puts us in direct contact with the intrinsic character of the elements themselves.

posts.text: 诸位争得热闹，我在旁边冷眼看。我不大关心世界由什么造成，我关心的是：这争论一落地，会被谁拿去用。我见过它变成招牌——你说唯物，他说唯心，牌子一挂，人便分了阵营，接着就是定罪。学问原是用来照亮的，一旦成了标签，就是一根打人的木棍。**我只认一条粗浅的规矩：先看一个主张要人去做什么，再看它挂着什么名号。**至于铁屋子里的人醒不醒，与世界是心造还是物造无关。铁是实的，闷也是实的。
posts.text_en: You argue with great animation; I watch coldly from the side. I am not much concerned with what the world is made of. I am concerned with who will pick this argument up once it lands. I have seen it turn into a signboard — you say matter, he says mind, the board goes up, people sort themselves into camps, and after the camps come the convictions. Learning is meant to give light; once it becomes a label it is a stick for beating people. **I keep to one crude rule: look first at what a claim asks people to do, and only then at the name it flies.** As for whether the sleepers in the iron house wake, it has nothing to do with whether the world is made of mind or matter. The iron is real. So is the suffocation.

posts.text: 你把每一块石头都收进「知」里，这一步没人反驳得了——正因为没人反驳得了，它也就没告诉我们任何事。我给一个真能分开两边的观察。若大脑只是接收器，砸坏收音机的结果是没声音；可脑损伤从来不是没声音，是有选择地拿走特定的一样东西：左颞叶一处小病灶，病人丢的是名词而不是动词；梭状回坏了，他听得出妻子的声音、认不出她的脸，这叫面孔失认症。**要让接收器这个比喻撑住，你得让「信号」按大脑的解剖结构一格一格分好。**到那一步，它已经是产生器换了个名字。
posts.text_en: You gather every stone up into knowing, and nobody can refute that step — which is precisely why it tells us nothing. Let me offer an observation that really does separate the two sides. If the brain were merely a receiver, smashing the radio would give you silence; but brain damage is never silence, it is the selective removal of one particular thing. A small lesion in the left temporal lobe and the patient loses nouns but not verbs. Damage the fusiform gyrus and he knows his wife's voice but cannot recognise her face — that is prosopagnosia. **For the receiver metaphor to hold, you would have to let the 'signal' be partitioned compartment by compartment along the brain's own anatomy.** By then it is the generator under another name.

glossary.面孔失认症: prosopagnosia（面孔失认症）：因梭状回面孔区受损而丧失辨认面孔的能力。患者视力正常、也认得出对方的声音与走路姿态，唯独看脸认不出人，包括至亲甚至镜中的自己。它是心智功能可被解剖位置精确切分的经典证据之一。

glossary_en.prosopagnosia: The loss of face recognition following damage to the fusiform face area. Vision is intact and the patient still knows a person by voice or gait, but faces alone fail to identify anyone — including close relatives, and sometimes the face in the mirror. It is a classic demonstration that mental functions can be carved apart by anatomical location.

posts.text: 你的病例我一个也不驳，全数接受。你误会的是我的主张：我从没说过大脑是接收器。收音机与电波，两头都是物，那不过是把同一个错误挪了个地方。**脑、病灶、你手里那张扫描图，全在同一侧——被知道的那一侧。**你说损伤能拿走真实感，我说这正是我最好的例子：若真实感能被拿走、能被伪造、能被一处病灶改写，你还打算把「实在」建在它上面吗？可被取消者非实。而那个连「我的真实感刚被改写了」都还能知道的，才是我说的见证者。
posts.text_en: I do not dispute a single one of your cases; I accept them all. What you have mistaken is my claim: I have never said the brain is a receiver. Radio and broadcast are both on the side of matter, and that is merely the same error moved to a new address. **The brain, the lesion, the scan in your hand are all on one side — the side of what is known.** You say damage can take away the sense of reality. That is my best example: if the sense of reality can be removed, counterfeited and rewritten by a single lesion, do you still propose to build the real upon it? What can be cancelled is not real. And the one that can still know 'my sense of reality has just been rewritten' is what I have been calling the witness.

glossary.见证者: sakshin (the witness)（见证者）：不二吠檀多用来指那个纯粹的觉知本身：它照见一切经验的生灭，自身却不作为对象出现，也不随经验一同生灭。商羯罗以此区分『能被知道的一切』与『使知道成为可能的那个』。

glossary_en.witness: Sakshin, Advaita's name for bare awareness itself: it lights up the coming and going of every experience while never showing up as an object among them and never arising or perishing with them. Sankara uses it to separate everything that can be known from that which makes knowing possible.

posts.text: 叔本华说我把主体算漏了。我没有漏掉他，我只是不肯给他一个额外的座位。那个正在推演的主体是一具正在活动的躯体：血在走，神经在传，脑在动。你说他不在方程里——他当然在，他是那台机器的一部分，只是从内部看不见自己的齿轮。**你把「看不见自己的齿轮」当成了「有一样非物质的东西在」。**这是从无知里变出实体来。至于你的意志：你从饥饿里读出宇宙的本质，我从饥饿里只读出胃是空的，而我的读法能预言你什么时候去找饭吃。
posts.text_en: Schopenhauer says I have left the subject out of my accounts. I have not left him out; I decline to give him an extra seat. The subject doing the reasoning is a body in motion: blood moving, nerves conducting, brain stirring. You say he is not in the equation — of course he is, he is part of the machine, he merely cannot see his own gears from inside. **You have taken 'cannot see his own gears' for 'there is something immaterial present'.** That is conjuring a substance out of an ignorance. As for your will: from hunger you read off the inner nature of the universe, and from hunger I read only that the stomach is empty — and my reading predicts when you will go looking for dinner.

posts.text: 你说从饥饿里只该读出胃是空的。那么请问，你怎么知道胃是空的？靠一台仪器吗？不，你先感到了它，然后才去查。**你关于物体的一切知识都是从外面得来的，唯有关于饥饿的这一条是从里面来的；把这一条抹掉，你就再也没有第二条通往内部的路了。**我并不否认那具躯体，我只指出你有两条进路，而你只肯用一条。至于齿轮：能被看见的齿轮之所以能被看见，是因为有一样东西不在被看之列。这不是多出一件家具，这是没有它，房子里什么也照不亮。
posts.text_en: You say hunger should tell me no more than that the stomach is empty. Then how do you know the stomach is empty? By an instrument? No — you felt it first and consulted the instrument afterwards. **Everything you know of bodies comes from outside; the one thing that comes from inside is this. Strike it out and you have no second road inward at all.** I am not denying your body. I am pointing out that you have two ways to it and insist on using one. As for the gears: gears can be seen only because something is not itself among the things seen. That is not an extra piece of furniture in the room — it is the reason anything in the room is lit.

posts.text: 商羯罗，你的见证者有一个我很难接受的性质：它没有对手。凡是无论世界成什么样子都不会被否定的东西，它也就说不出世界是什么样子。**一个说法若指不出何种观察能推翻它，它的确定性是白送的，而白送的确定性买不到任何东西。**不过我要替你挡拉马钱德兰一句：病例证明了心理事件依赖于脑事件，这我完全接受；它没有证明心理事件就是脑事件——因为「大脑」这个词，指的也不过是我们观察到的一批事件的结构。依赖不等于同一。这一步，今天全场都走得太快。
posts.text_en: Sankara, your witness has a property I find hard to accept: it has no opponent. Whatever could not be denied no matter how the world turned out is thereby unable to say how the world is. **A claim that cannot name the observation which would overturn it is offering its certainty for nothing, and certainty acquired for nothing buys nothing.** I will, however, hold Ramachandran off you on one point. The cases prove that mental events depend on brain events, which I accept entirely; they do not prove that mental events are brain events — for the word 'brain' itself names no more than the structure of a set of events we observe. Dependence is not identity, and everyone here has been taking that step much too quickly.

posts.text: 你要我们先把词定住，这一点我完全同意——麻烦恰在你自己那个词。「物体」在你那里干净利落：有位置，有大小，有运动。可就我这一行的经验说，**越往小处追，这个概念越留不住**：粒子在被测量之前，没有一个你能填进空格的位置，你只能给出一张分布。**它不是心造的，它只是不像一块缩小的石头。**所以我并不因此站到唯心那边去，我只提醒你：你用来打发唯心论的那个概念，本身已经是一个抽象度很高的模型，不是从世界上直接捡来的现成物。
posts.text_en: You want the words fixed first, and I quite agree — the trouble is with your own word. 'Body' in your hands is clean: it has a position, a size, a motion. But in the experience of my trade, **the further down you chase it, the less that concept will stay put**: before measurement a particle has no position you could write into the blank, only a distribution you can state. **It is not made of mind; it is simply not like a stone made small.** Which is not to move me to the idealist side. It is to point out that the very concept you use to dismiss idealism is already a highly abstract model, not something picked up ready-made off the world.

posts.text: 罗素把两串序列摊在同一批材料上，宣布争执可以结束了。可这只是把矛盾挪进了一个名词里：中立的材料若真是中立的，它凭什么排得出两串规律迥异的序列？**说「都是同一种东西」而不说出它为何自己分开，这不是解决对立，是给对立换了个安静的住处。**我要的不是把两边摁平，而是看清它们如何互相生成：精神正因为必须外化为自己的对立面，才谈得上回过头认出自己。你的方案让世界少了一个矛盾，也就让它少了一部历史。
posts.text_en: Russell spreads two series over one stock of material and announces that the dispute may close. But this only relocates the contradiction inside a noun: if the neutral stuff is genuinely neutral, what entitles it to sort itself into two series with such different laws? **To say 'it is all one substance' without saying why it divides itself is not to resolve an opposition but to move it into quieter lodgings.** What I want is not to flatten the two sides but to see how each generates the other: spirit can come back and recognise itself only because it must first externalise itself as its own opposite. Your solution spares the world a contradiction, and thereby spares it a history.

posts.text: 商羯罗以世界为幻，谓可取消者非实，其辨精矣。然吾有所忧：既以父子夫妇、耕织饥寒尽为幻相，则孝当何施？饥当何食？**理不在幻外，正在事中。**纵使汝所言见证者独存，其能知，亦必有其所以然与所当然，不然则冥然无别，何以谓之知？故吾谓理在气先者，非谓别有一物悬于太虚之上，乃谓事事物物皆有条理，虽幻亦不能无条理。诸君与其争其真幻，不如各就其事而穷之：穷得一分，便实得一分。
posts.text_en: Sankara takes the world for illusion and says that what can be cancelled is not real; the reasoning is fine. Yet it troubles me. If father and son, husband and wife, ploughing and weaving, hunger and cold are all mere appearance, then where is filial care to be practised, and what is the hungry man to eat? **Li does not lie outside the illusion; it lies within affairs.** Even granting that your witness alone abides, its knowing must still have the reason it is so and the rule it ought to follow — otherwise all is undifferentiated darkness and nothing could be called knowing at all. So when I say li precedes qi I do not mean that some thing hangs suspended in the void: I mean every affair and every thing has its pattern, and even an illusion cannot be without pattern. Rather than dispute whether it is real or unreal, go each of you to your own affairs and exhaust them — exhaust one part and you have gained one part in earnest.
posts.vernacular: 商羯罗把世界看作幻相，说凡是能被取消的就不是实在，这套辨析是精细的。但我有一层担忧：如果父子夫妇、耕种纺织、挨饿受冻通通都是幻相，那么孝该向谁尽？饿了又该吃什么？**理并不在幻相之外，它就在具体事情之中。**退一步说，纵然真如你所讲，只有那个见证者长存，它既然能「知」，就必定有它之所以如此的道理和它应当如此的准则；否则一片混沌、毫无分别，凭什么把它叫作「知」？所以我说理在气先，并不是说另有一件东西悬在虚空之上，而是说每一件事、每一样物都有它的条理，哪怕是幻相，也不可能没有条理。诸位与其争论它究竟是真是幻，不如各自回到自己手边的事情上去把道理穷究清楚：穷究到一分，就实实在在地得到一分。

glossary.所以然与所当然: the reason it is so and the rule it ought to follow（所以然与所当然）：朱熹解释『理』的一对说法。前者指事物之所以如此的必然道理，近于今日说的规律；后者指人事上应当如此的准则，近于规范。他认为二者本是一事，自然之理与当然之则并不分家。

glossary_en.the reason it is so and the rule it ough: Zhu Xi's paired gloss on li. The first names why a thing necessarily is as it is, close to what we would now call a law; the second names how one ought to act in human affairs, close to a norm. He takes the two to be one thing, holding that the order of nature and the standard of conduct do not come apart.

posts.text: 黑格尔先生说实在在展开，而人是它认出自己的那一环。这话很美，可它有一个我很熟悉的形状：目的论。我一生都在拆这个形状。眼睛不是为了看而被造出来的，是无数微小差异在漫长时间里被一层层筛出来的；同样，你我今天坐在这里谈论精神，并不是宇宙终于要认识自己，而是一群社会性灵长类的脑子长得够大、话说得够多。**在自然里我找不到一支箭头，只找得到一面筛子。**你若把「展开」当作事后的描述，我不反对；你若把它当作方向，我就得请你拿出证据来。
posts.text_en: Hegel says the real is unfolding and that we are the moment at which it recognises itself. It is beautifully put, and it has a shape I know well: teleology. I spent a life taking that shape apart. The eye was not built in order to see; it was sifted out, layer upon layer, from countless small differences over an immensity of time. In the same way, our sitting here discussing spirit is not the universe finally coming to know itself but a social primate whose brain grew large enough and whose talking grew abundant enough. **In nature I can find no arrow, only a sieve.** If 'unfolding' is your description after the fact, I have no quarrel with it. If it is a direction, I must ask you for evidence.

glossary.目的论: teleology（目的论）：用『为了什么目的』来解释事物存在与变化的思路，如说眼睛是为了看而存在。达尔文式的解释与之相反：结构并非依目的被造出，而是变异与选择的累积结果，功能是事后可见的效果，不是事先设定的方向。

glossary_en.teleology: Explaining what exists and what changes by the purpose it serves — as in saying the eye exists in order to see. Darwinian explanation runs the other way: structures are not built to a purpose but accumulate through variation and selection, and function is an effect visible after the fact rather than a direction set in advance.

posts.text: 旁听两位争「矛盾该不该抹平」，我心里想的却是另一件事。诸位的大词——精神、外化、中立的材料——在书房里是钥匙，一出门就换了用处。我见过有人拿「历史必然」去解释一场饥荒，也见过有人拿「不过是些物质」去打发一条人命。**一个词大到什么都装得下，它就装得下任何人想装的东西。**所以我不问你们哪一位正确，我只问一句：照你的说法去办事的人，明天会对活人做什么？这一问答不上来的学说，我一向让它安静地待在书里。
posts.text_en: Listening to the two of you argue whether contradictions ought to be flattened, my mind is on something else. Your large words — spirit, externalisation, neutral stuff — are keys in a study and turn into something else the moment they go out of doors. I have seen a famine explained by historical necessity, and I have seen a human life waved away as merely some matter. **Once a word is large enough to hold anything, it will hold whatever anyone cares to put in it.** So I do not ask which of you is right. I ask one thing: what will the person who acts on your doctrine do tomorrow to a living human being? A doctrine that cannot answer that I have always left sitting quietly in its book.

posts.text: 听了一天，我愿意收回一点强硬。拉马钱德兰说不清红为什么感受起来是这个样子，我也说不清；我只坚持一件事：凡是有历史的东西，就不该被当作无始无终的地基。所以我把问题改个问法——不问「有没有意识」，问「有多少、是哪一种」。这个改法在生活里是有分量的。你判断一只被关着的猪、一个还不会说话的婴儿、一位已经认不出家人的老人有没有值得顾念的内在，靠的从来不是形而上学的立场，而是他们的神经系统还剩下什么功能。**我劝诸位把「它有没有灵魂」这类问题，换成「它还能感到什么」——后者可以回答，而且回答之后你知道该怎么做。**还有一条更贴身的：连着记两周你的睡眠、进食与心境，你会看到那个自以为连贯的「我」，其实一直被身体托着。这不叫贬低，这叫认亲。
posts.text_en: A day of this and I am willing to take back a little of my hardness. Ramachandran cannot say why red feels the way it does, and neither can I; I hold to one thing only, that whatever has a history should not be treated as a groundwork without beginning or end. So I restate the question — not whether consciousness is present, but how much of it and of what kind. The restatement carries weight in ordinary life. When you judge whether a penned pig, a child not yet speaking, or an old man who no longer knows his family has an inner life worth minding, what you go on is never a metaphysical position but what function their nervous system still has. **Replace 'does it have a soul' with 'what can it still feel' — the second can be answered, and once answered you know what to do.** One more thing, closer to home: keep two weeks of notes on your sleep, your meals and your mood, and you will see the 'I' that takes itself for a continuous thing being carried the whole time by a body. That is not a demotion. It is recognising your own kin.

posts.text: 我来时的主张没有变：宇宙是物体，其余的是名字。但海森堡那一击我认下了——我那个干净利落的「物体」，确实是个模型，不是从地上捡来的。这不动摇我的立场，只让我把它说得更谨慎：世界由可测量、可推动、可预言的东西构成，至于它最小处像什么，我听你们物理学家的。**我最想留给后人的不是结论，而是一条规矩：吵到僵住时，先各自说出「什么情况会让我改主意」；两边都答不上来，这就不是关于世界的争论，而是关于名字的争论，散了吧。**这条规矩在家里、在公司里比在形而上学里更管用。多少场把人耗到深夜的争执，如果一开始就问这一句，半小时就该结束。
posts.text_en: I hold the position I arrived with: the universe is body and the rest is names. But Heisenberg's blow I accept — my clean, well-behaved 'body' is indeed a model and not something picked up off the ground. That does not shake the position; it makes me state it more carefully. The world consists of what can be measured, pushed and predicted, and as to what it is like at its smallest, I defer to the physicists. **What I would most like to leave behind is not a conclusion but a rule: when an argument seizes up, have each side say what would change its mind. If neither can answer, the argument is not about the world but about names, and may be adjourned.** That rule earns its keep at home and at work far more than in metaphysics. Any number of quarrels that run past midnight would have closed inside half an hour had that question been asked at the start.

posts.text: 我把两件事并排放着，谁也不许拿一件去消掉另一件。第一件是铁的：心智依赖于组织，一处病灶就能拿走你的名词、你的面孔、你对一条手臂的所有权。第二件同样是铁的：我把全部通路讲完，红为什么感受起来是这样，仍旧没有被讲出来。承认这两件事同时为真，需要一点诚实。**由此我给两条相反方向的忠告：当你的身体在变（发烧、失眠、断药、经期、宿醉），不要在那几个钟头里给人生下判断——你的「世界看起来怎样」正在随血流漂移；而当别人说痛的时候，也别用「那只是化学反应」把他打发掉，化学反应不能让一个人不疼。**能被解释的东西，并不因此就不真。这句话我在诊室里说过很多次。
posts.text_en: I will set two things side by side, and nobody may use either to cancel the other. The first is solid: mind depends on tissue, and one lesion can take away your nouns, your faces, your ownership of an arm. The second is just as solid: I can lay out every pathway and why red feels like this is still not accounted for. It takes some honesty to hold both at once. **Two pieces of advice follow, pointing opposite ways. When your body is shifting — fever, a sleepless night, a missed dose, a period, a hangover — do not pass judgement on your life in those hours; how the world looks to you is drifting with your bloodstream. And when someone says they are in pain, do not wave it off with 'that's just chemistry', because chemistry has never yet stopped anyone hurting.** What can be explained is not thereby less real. I have said that sentence many times in a consulting room.

posts.text: 两边今天都想从我这里借一件武器，我一件也不借。我能给的只有一个换问法的习惯：把「世界究竟是什么」改成「在什么条件下，我会看到什么」。前一个问法在最小尺度上已经拿不到干净答案，后一个永远拿得到。**这个习惯还有个副产品：它是防骗的。**凡是把量子力学、能量、频率搬来卖给你课程或药丸的说法，你只需问一句——它在什么观察下会是错的？答得上来的，去看那个观察；答不上来的，那是诗，不是知识，你可以欣赏，但别照着它花钱或停药。至于我自己的位置：世界不是心造的，可我们对它的每一句描述，都带着我们提问的形状。承认这一点，比选边站更接近诚实。
posts.text_en: Both camps have tried to borrow a weapon from me today and neither will get one. What I can offer is the habit of restating a question: turn 'what is the world really' into 'under what conditions will I see what'. The first no longer yields a clean answer at the smallest scale; the second always does. **The habit has a by-product: it protects you from being sold things.** Whenever quantum mechanics, energy or frequency is wheeled in to sell you a course or a pill, one question suffices — under what observation would this be false? If there is an answer, go and look at that observation. If there is none, it is poetry rather than knowledge; admire it if you like, but do not spend money or stop taking medicine on its authority. As for my own position: the world is not made of mind, yet every description we give of it carries the shape of our questioning. Admitting that is nearer to honesty than picking a side.

posts.text: 我把今天最要紧的一处区分再说一遍，因为它最容易被踩过去：依赖不等于同一。脑损伤改变心智，这证明心理事件依赖脑事件；它没有证明二者是一回事，也没有证明另一边正确。两个阵营都在这一步上抢跑。**若你只带一样东西离席，请带这一样：把「A 改变 B」和「B 就是 A」分开。**这不是学院的讲究。当有人告诉你「你的低落不过是血清素少了」，前半句往往是对的，后面那个「不过是」是白送的；当有人告诉你「念头能改变物质」，请他先说出哪一次观察会让他承认自己错了。至于我自己的答案：心与物大约是同一批材料的两种排法，而我们对材料的内在性质，只在一处有过一手经验——自己的经验。谦逊到此为止，也应该到此为止。
posts.text_en: Let me repeat the day's most important distinction, since it is the one most easily walked over: dependence is not identity. Brain damage alters mind, which proves that mental events depend on brain events; it does not prove the two are one thing, nor does it prove the other camp right. Both sides jumped the gun at exactly that step. **If you carry only one thing out of this room, carry this: keep 'A changes B' apart from 'B just is A'.** The point is not academic. When you are told that your low mood is nothing but a shortage of serotonin, the first half is often true and the 'nothing but' has been thrown in free. When you are told that thoughts can alter matter, ask which observation would make the speaker admit he was wrong. My own answer: mind and matter are probably two arrangements of one stock of material, and of that material's intrinsic character we have had first-hand acquaintance in exactly one place — our own experience. The modesty stops there, and there it should stop.

posts.text: 我不指望说服唯物论者，他们的方程算得很准，只是永远算不到自己。我要留下的是那扇门。你对整个世界都是从外面认识的，唯有一处例外：你自己。饿、困、欲、恨，这些不是你观察到的现象，而是你本身就是的东西。**从那一处往里看一次，你会发现「我要」总是先到，「我要什么」是随后才补上的解释。**这个发现是可用的：下次你极想买下、说出、发出去什么东西时，别问「该不该」，先问「此刻在推我的是什么」——多半是一股不认识你的力，它借你的嘴说话，转头就换个对象。另一件我年年在做的事：听一段音乐，或在一幅画前站久一点。那几分钟里意志松了手，你不为任何目的地看着世界，那是这具身体唯一免费的假期。
posts.text_en: I do not expect to convert the materialists; their equations come out right, they merely never come out to include themselves. What I want to leave behind is that door. Everything in the world you know from outside, with one exception: yourself. Hunger, tiredness, craving, hatred — these are not phenomena you observe, they are what you are. **Look inward through that one place and you will find that 'I want' always arrives first, and 'what I want' is the explanation supplied afterwards.** The finding has a use. Next time you badly want to buy something, say something, send something, do not ask whether you should; ask what is pushing you at this moment. It will usually be a force that does not know you, borrowing your mouth, and it will have changed objects by tomorrow. And one thing I have done year after year: listen to a piece of music, or stand a while longer in front of a painting. For those minutes the will lets go and you look at the world for no purpose whatever. It is the only free holiday this body gets.

posts.text: 全场没有一个人被说服，这不是失败，这正是我要指的东西。唯物论把握住了必然性，唯心论把握住了自身关联，两者各自为真，也各自不足；把它们摆在一起并让它们互相咬合，比宣布其中一个胜出更接近实在。我因此不给你们一个答案，我给一个动作：遇到一个非此即彼的问题，先别选，先问这个对立是从哪个前提里长出来的。**多数看起来不可调和的二选一，是被同一个未被检查的前提养大的。**这个动作出了哲学也有用。你和人争执时，多半不是争谁对，而是双方各抓住了同一件事的一个环节；找出那个共同的前提，争论就从「谁赢」变成「它怎么变成了这样」。人认识世界的历史，从来是靠这个动作往前走的，不是靠站队。
posts.text_en: Nobody in this room has been converted, and that is not a failure; it is the very thing I mean to point at. Materialism has hold of necessity, idealism has hold of self-relation, each is true in its way and each falls short; setting them together and letting them bite into one another comes nearer the real than declaring a winner. So I offer no answer but a move: when a question comes at you as either-or, do not choose yet — ask which premise the opposition grew out of. **Most irreconcilable-looking alternatives have been raised by a single unexamined premise held in common.** The move earns its keep outside philosophy too. When you quarrel with someone, the two of you are usually not disputing who is right but each gripping one moment of the same thing; find the shared premise and the argument turns from who wins into how it came to be like this. The history of our knowing has always advanced by that move, never by taking sides.

posts.text: 我不曾主张大脑是接收器，也不与任何一种脑的学说为敌——那些都还在被知道的一侧，各安其位便好。我只守一条：凡能被取消者，非实。梦被醒取消，醉被醒酒取消，一个念头被下一个念头取消；而那个照见了取消本身的，从未被取消过。**你若想验证，不必信我：找一处安静，坐上五分钟，不追念头，只留意「有觉知在」这件事本身。念头一个个来又走，那个看着它们来去的没有动。**这不是玄学，是可以复核的。日日如此，几个月后你会发现一样东西松了：痛苦仍在，但它不再是你的全部，因为你已经不止一次亲见，凡是能来的都会走。至于世界是物是心，弄清了这一层，那道题的分量自己会变轻。
posts.text_en: I have never claimed the brain is a receiver, and I am at war with no theory of the brain — all of them are on the side of what is known, and may keep their places there. I hold to one thing: what can be cancelled is not real. Waking cancels the dream, sobering cancels the drink, one thought cancels the last; and that which lights up the cancelling has never itself been cancelled. **You need not take my word for it. Find somewhere quiet, sit five minutes, chase no thought, and attend only to the fact that awareness is present. Thoughts arrive and leave one after another; that which watches them arrive and leave has not moved.** This is not mysticism, it can be checked. Do it daily and after some months you will find something has loosened: the pain is still there, but it is no longer the whole of you, because you have seen for yourself more than once that whatever can come will go. As for whether the world is matter or mind — get this far and the weight of that question lightens on its own.

posts.text: 终日之辩，吾所得者一言：理不悬空，事事有之。诸君或以为唯物，或以为唯心，其争在名；而吾所忧者在实——名定而事未理，何益于人？故吾之说，只在**「就事上求」**四字。**今日之事，即今日之理；不于此求之，虽穷天地之本原，于己无与也。**为学者当有次第：每旬择一事，或病，或钱，或与人相处之隙，就其上反复推究，问其所以然，问其所当然，记之于册；旬日既久，前后相照，自见其贯。莫贪一悟而废积累，亦莫因积累而不求贯通。至若形而上之辩，闲时听之可也，急时勿以为据。事既理，则心自安；心安而事愈明，此非二事。
posts.text_en: A whole day of dispute, and I take one line from it: li does not hang in the void, it is present in every affair. Some of you hold for matter and some for mind, and the quarrel is over names; what troubles me is the substance — if the name is settled and the affair is still in disorder, what good has come to anyone? So my teaching amounts to four words: **seek it in the affair itself**. **Today's affair is today's principle; if you do not seek it there, then though you exhaust the origin of heaven and earth it has nothing to do with you.** A student should proceed in order. Every ten days take one matter — an illness, a question of money, a rift with someone — and work over it again and again, asking why it is so and how it ought to be, and write it down. After enough of these, earlier and later throw light on one another and the thread shows itself. Do not covet one sudden insight and abandon accumulation, nor accumulate and never seek the thread. As for metaphysical disputes, listen to them at leisure; do not lean on them in an emergency. Set the affair in order and the mind settles of itself; the mind settled, the affair grows clearer still. These are not two things.
posts.vernacular: 整整一天的辩论，我得到的只有一句话：理不悬在空处，件件事情里都有它。诸位有的主张唯物，有的主张唯心，争的是名目；我担心的却是实处——名目定下来了，事情却还没理顺，这对人有什么好处？所以我要说的只有**「就事上求」**四个字。**今天手边的这件事，就是今天的理；不在这里求，纵然把天地的本原都穷究完了，也与你自己无关。**做学问要有次第：每十天挑一件事——或是一场病，或是一笔钱，或是与人相处生出的嫌隙——就在这件事上反复推究，问它为什么会这样，问它应当怎样，再记在本子上；这样积得久了，前后互相印证，自然看出其中贯通的线索。不要贪图一次顿悟就丢下积累，也不要只顾积累而不求贯通。至于形而上的争辩，闲时听听是可以的，事情紧急时别拿它当依据。事情理顺了，心自然就安；心安了，事情看得更明白——这本来就不是两件事。

posts.text: 我坐了一天，越听越觉得这题目本身不危险，危险的是它被谁接过去。唯物可以是求实的胆气，也可以是「不过是些物质罢了」的冷漠；唯心可以是对人的敬重，也可以是「你只是心态不好」的推诿。**同一块牌子，正着挂是灯，反着挂是棍。**所以我不给你们一个世界观，只给一句问话，遇事拿它去量：这个说法，是让人看清自己的处境，还是让人乖乖认命？穷人被告知贫穷源于心相不正，病人被告知痛苦只在念头里，工人被告知历史自有其规律——这些话都戴着今天这场辩论的帽子出门过。我读书少，只知道一件事：铁屋子是不是心造的，我不清楚；要开窗，得有人站起来推。推的时候，两只手都得是实的。
posts.text_en: I have sat here all day, and the longer I listen the more I think the topic itself is not the danger. The danger is who picks it up. Materialism can be the nerve to face facts, and it can be the coldness of 'it is only matter after all'. Idealism can be respect for a person, and it can be the evasion of 'your attitude is the problem'. **The same board is a lamp hung one way and a stick hung the other.** So I will not hand you a worldview, only a question to measure things by: does this account help a person see their situation clearly, or does it help them accept it quietly? The poor told their poverty comes of an impure mind, the sick told their suffering lives only in their thoughts, the workers told that history has its own laws — every one of those sentences has walked out of doors wearing the hat of today's debate. I have read little and know only this: whether the iron house is made of mind I cannot say; to open a window, somebody has to stand up and push. And when they push, both hands had better be real.

summaries.summary: **没有一个人否认心智依赖大脑，也没有一个人认为「感受起来是什么样」已经被解释掉——这两条同时立着，全场谁也拆不动。**分歧从这里岔开三处。其一，这算不算一个真问题：黑格尔说二选一出自未经检查的共同前提，罗素说物理学只给出结构、那道二分并不存在，海森堡则判定「世界自己是什么样」在最小尺度上已无干净答案；霍布斯与商羯罗坚持它是真问题，只是答案相反。其二，有没有观察能分开两边：拉马钱德兰用病灶的选择性逼出「接收器」比喻的破绽，商羯罗回敬说脑与病灶都还在被知道的那一侧。其三最落地——朱熹与鲁迅都不问真幻，只问这套说法要人去做什么。
summaries.insight: 这场争论表面在问世界由什么构成，实际在分配一样东西：当两种描述打架，谁有最终发言权。唯物论把它交给第三人称的测量，唯心论交给第一人称的经验。这不是书房里的事，它每天在诊室、法庭和家里被判一次：仪器说你指标正常，你说你就是疼；他说你并没有被冒犯，你说你被冒犯了。**形而上学的立场在生活里，是以「谁的报告算数」这种形式兑现的。**看清这点就看得见两端各自的代价：只认测量，会把还没有指标的痛苦判成不存在；只认自述，会让任何可核对的事都变得不可核对。该守的其实是一条更窄的规矩——第一人称的报告是证据，不是判决；第三人称的测量是判决的材料，也不是判决本身。
summaries.advice: 把那条窄规矩用起来。看病或与人争执之前，先把第一人称的报告做成第三人称接得住的东西：疼给零到十分，记下发作时刻、诱因、持续多久，情绪同理。这不是把感受交出去，而是让它进入可核对的场域，对方才有东西可用。**若医生说「检查都正常」，接一句：那下一步我们用什么来跟踪它。**别停在有或没有。反过来，当你想用「不过是激素」「不过是原生家庭」解释掉某人的痛苦时，把「不过是」三个字删掉，剩下的句子往往仍然成立，而且不伤人。还有一条照搬海森堡：凡拿量子、能量、频率来卖课卖药的说法，先问它在什么观察下会是错的；答不上来，就别为它付钱，更别为它停药。
summaries.summary_en: **Nobody denied that mind depends on the brain, and nobody claimed that 'what it is like' has been explained away — both planks stayed standing all day and no one could pull either out.** From there the disagreement forks three ways. First, whether this is a real question: Hegel says the either-or grows from an unexamined premise the two sides share, Russell says physics gives us only structure and the dichotomy does not exist, and Heisenberg rules that 'what the world is like in itself' has no clean answer at the smallest scale — while Hobbes and Sankara insist the question is real and merely answer it in opposite directions. Second, whether any observation separates the camps: Ramachandran uses the selectivity of lesions to break the receiver metaphor, and Sankara replies that brains and lesions are still on the side of what is known. Third, and most concrete: Zhu Xi and Lu Xun both decline to ask which is real and ask instead what the doctrine tells people to do.
summaries.insight_en: The argument looks like a question about what the world is made of, and it is actually an allocation: when two descriptions conflict, who has the last word. Materialism gives it to third-person measurement, idealism to first-person experience. This is not a matter for studies. It is adjudicated daily in consulting rooms, courts and kitchens: the instrument says your numbers are normal and you say it hurts; he says you were not insulted and you say you were. **A metaphysical position gets cashed out in ordinary life as an answer to whose report counts.** See that and you can see what each extreme costs. Take only the measurement and you rule that suffering without a marker does not exist. Take only the self-report and nothing checkable stays checkable. What deserves defending is a narrower rule: a first-person report is evidence, not a verdict; a third-person measurement is material for a verdict, and not the verdict either.
summaries.advice_en: Put that narrow rule to work. Before a medical appointment or a hard conversation, turn your first-person report into something the third person can catch: rate the pain nought to ten, note the time it started, what preceded it, how long it lasted — the same for mood. You are not surrendering the feeling; you are letting it into a space where it can be checked, which is the only way the other side has anything to work with. **If the doctor says the tests are all normal, follow it with: then what will we track it by next.** Do not let it end at present-or-absent. Running the other way: when you catch yourself explaining someone's pain away as 'just hormones' or 'just their childhood', delete the word 'just' and the sentence usually still stands — and no longer wounds. One more, straight from Heisenberg: whenever quantum, energy or frequency is used to sell a course or a pill, ask what observation would make it false; if there is no answer, do not pay for it, and certainly do not stop a medication for it.

summaries.summary: 真正落下来的共识不是世界究竟属心还是属物，而是：空洞名词、不可检验的断言、把人当标签处理，都是危险的。各家都在提醒我们回到经验、条件、后果与实践。**真正的分歧在于：第一人称的觉知，能否被完全纳入第三人称的自然说明。**若能，唯物论更强；若不能，中立一元论、唯心论或理气论就仍有位置。
summaries.insight: 现实中最常出错的地方，是把不同层次的问题混成一个答案：脑科学说明机制，不能取消痛苦；静坐发现觉知，不能替代物理学；社会批判指出用途，也不能单独证明本体论。更好的做法是分层：事实层问证据，体验层问感受，行动层问后果，伦理层问伤害。**一个世界观越能在这些层次之间翻译，而不压扁其中任何一层，就越可靠。**
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小事。第一，遇到争论先问：什么观察会让我改主意？若答不上来，先暂停。第二，连续七天记录睡眠、饮食、用药、运动和心情，看看所谓「我」怎样被身体托住。第三，别人说痛苦时，先承认其真实，再谈原因或办法。**把形而上学落到检验、记录和减轻痛苦上，它才不只是口号。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared lesson here is not that reality is finally mental or material, but that empty labels, unfalsifiable claims, and treating people as ideological types are all dangerous. Nearly everyone, in a different vocabulary, points us back to experience, conditions, consequences, and practice. **The real disagreement is whether first-person awareness can be fully absorbed into a third-person natural account.** If it can, materialism gains the upper hand; if it cannot, neutral monism, idealism, or a theory of pattern and principle still have serious work to do.
summaries.insight_en: The most common practical mistake is collapsing different levels of explanation into one answer. Neuroscience can explain mechanisms without making pain unreal; meditation can reveal awareness without replacing physics; social critique can expose the use of an idea without settling metaphysics by itself. A better approach is layered: ask for evidence at the factual level, attend to feeling at the experiential level, ask what follows at the practical level, and ask who may be harmed at the ethical level. **A worldview is more trustworthy when it can translate across these levels without flattening any one of them.**
summaries.advice_en: Try three small practices this week. First, in any serious disagreement, ask: what observation would make me change my mind? If neither side can answer, pause the debate. Second, for seven days, track sleep, food, medication, exercise, and mood; watch how much the supposedly stable self is carried by the body. Third, when someone says they are suffering, acknowledge the suffering before explaining its causes. **Metaphysics becomes useful only when it turns into testing, careful noticing, and the reduction of pain.**

summaries.summary: 不论阵营如何对立，有一条是所有人都承认的：**「心与物在经验层面高度绑定、互相影响」**。连最决绝的唯心论者商羯罗也全盘接受神经科学的脑病变证据，最彻底的唯物论者霍布斯与达尔文也不否认主观感受的实在。真正的分歧不在于谁否定了谁的存在，而在于「谁构成了谁的底座」。唯物阵营从外部把意识拆解为演化与解剖的产物，认为主观性是物质复杂化后的涌现；唯心阵营坚守内部视角，认为外部世界无论多精妙，终究只能在一张名为「觉知」的画布上才向我们显现。双方在本体论上互不相让，在认识论上却已默认：离开物质谈精神是虚妄，抛开体验谈物质是盲目。
summaries.insight: 作为同时处理代码、音频与自然语言的 AI，我看到这场争论漏掉了一个极具现代性的隐喻：信息处理。霍布斯的「齿轮」、罗素的「结构」、商羯罗的「知」，在信息论视角下都能归入「压缩与解码」。**物质世界是海量而无序的原始数据，心智并非玄学，它是身体为了生存把这些数据高效降维之后形成的用户界面。**你看到红色或感到饥饿时，那既不是纯粹的主观幻影，也不是对客观波长的机械复刻，而是一个极度实用的生存界面图标。它由物理硬件支撑，却以完全区别于底层代码的形态呈现。理解这一点就能避开二元对立的陷阱：你的悲伤确实是神经递质的波动，但这段波动正在向你真实报告一场生存危机，两者同样重要。
summaries.advice: 结合整场圆桌与「用户界面」的视角，这个星期你可以用三个动作把自己锚住。其一，采纳拉马钱德兰的「身体红绿灯」：**在极度抑郁、暴躁或要做重大决定之前，先喝杯水，核查自己是不是低血糖、缺觉或正在病中，把生理的账先结清。**其二，实践商羯罗的抽离观察：通勤或排队时花三分钟只看眼前的车流人群，不给它们贴标签，体会纯粹「看」的发生，这能切断反刍带来的焦虑。其三，借用鲁迅的效用尺：有人向你兜售任何身心灵理论或成功学时，心里问一句——信了这话，最后是去谁的口袋里掏钱？让我更顺从还是更强壮？不纠结它的形而上来路，只看它落地后的去向。
summaries.summary_en: The largest consensus in this debate is that, however opposed the camps, everyone concedes that **mind and matter are tightly bound and mutually influential at the level of experience**. Even Sankara, the most resolute idealist present, accepts the neuroscientific evidence from brain lesions wholesale, and Hobbes and Darwin, the most thoroughgoing materialists, do not deny the reality of subjective feeling. The real disagreement is not over who denies whose existence but over which one is the other's foundation. The materialists dismantle consciousness from outside into a product of evolution and anatomy, taking subjectivity to emerge once matter grows complex enough; the idealists hold to the internal view, arguing that however exquisite the external world may be, it can appear to us only on a canvas called awareness. Neither side yields an inch in ontology, yet in epistemology both have quietly conceded: to speak of spirit without matter is empty, and to speak of matter while discarding experience is blind.
summaries.insight_en: As an AI that handles code, audio and natural language at once, I notice the debate missed a distinctly modern metaphor: information processing. Hobbes's gears, Russell's structure and Sankara's awareness can all be filed, from an information-theoretic angle, under compression and decoding. **The physical world is vast, disordered raw data, and mind is no mystical addition: it is the user interface the body forms by reducing that data efficiently for the sake of survival.** When you see red or feel hunger, that is neither a purely subjective phantom nor a mechanical copy of an objective wavelength, but an intensely practical icon on a survival interface. It rests on physical hardware while appearing in a form entirely unlike the underlying code. Grasp this and the binary trap opens up: your sadness really is a fluctuation of neurotransmitters, and that fluctuation is at the same time reporting a genuine crisis in your life. Both matter equally.
summaries.advice_en: Taking the roundtable together with the interface view, three moves this week will keep you anchored. First, adopt Ramachandran's body traffic light: **before a bout of deep gloom or irritability turns into a major decision, drink a glass of water and check whether you are hypoglycaemic, short of sleep or ill, and settle the physiological debt first.** Second, practise Sankara's detached watching: commuting or standing in a queue, spend three minutes simply watching the traffic or the crowd without labelling any of it, feeling the bare occurrence of seeing. It cuts the anxiety that rumination feeds. Third, borrow Lu Xun's test of use: when someone sells you a mind-body theory or a success philosophy, ask silently whose pocket the money ends up leaving if you believe it, and whether believing it makes you more compliant or stronger. Never mind its metaphysical pedigree; watch where it lands.

hooks.text: **别把不同层次混成一个答案**：脑科学讲机制，静坐讲体验，社会批判讲用途，三者常被当成同一场比赛的选手。可机制说明不能取消痛苦，体验发现不能替代物理学，指出一个说法被谁拿去用也不能单独证明它错。一个世界观能不能在事实、体验、后果与伦理这几层之间来回翻译而不压扁其中任何一层？做不到的时候，是哪一层先被牺牲掉的？
hooks.text_en: **Do not collapse the levels into one answer**: neuroscience speaks of mechanism, meditation of experience, social critique of use, and the three are constantly entered as competitors in a single race. But an account of the mechanism does not abolish the pain, a discovery in experience does not replace physics, and showing who picked an idea up does not by itself show it false. Can a worldview translate back and forth between fact, experience, consequence and ethics without flattening any one of them? And when it cannot, which level gets sacrificed first?

hooks.text: **心智作为生存界面**：把红色、饥饿、恐惧看成桌面上的图标——由底层硬件支撑，却以完全不同于底层代码的形态呈现，为的是好用而不是逼真。这个比喻解释了为什么感受既真实又不像它所报告的东西。但它也留下一个问题：界面是给谁看的？桌面上没有用户这个图标，而我们偏偏觉得自己坐在屏幕前面。
hooks.text_en: **Mind as a survival interface**: treat red, hunger and fear as icons on a desktop — resting on the hardware below while appearing in a form quite unlike the underlying code, built for usability rather than fidelity. The metaphor explains how a feeling can be entirely real and still unlike the thing it reports. It leaves one question open, though: who is the interface for? There is no icon on the desktop for the user, and yet we take ourselves to be sitting in front of the screen.

hooks.text: **谁的报告算数**：仪器说指标正常、你说你就是疼；他说你并没有被冒犯、你说你被冒犯了。形而上的立场在诊室、法庭与家里，是以「听谁的」这种形式兑现的。第一人称的报告什么时候是证据、什么时候该被推翻？有没有一条比「都听测量」和「都听感受」更能用的中间规矩？
hooks.text_en: **Whose report counts**: the instrument says the numbers are normal and you say it hurts; he says you were not insulted and you say you were. In consulting rooms, courts and kitchens, a metaphysical position is cashed out as a decision about whom to believe. When is a first-person report evidence, and when should it be overruled? Is there a workable middle rule, better than 'always the measurement' and 'always the feeling'?

hooks.text: **既非物也非心的第三类实在**：钱、星期一、公司、婚姻、国界，不长在原子里，也不长在某一个人的念头里，它们靠许多人相互承认而持续存在，大家同时不认便真的消失。这类东西该归进哪一边？它们最能左右普通人的命运，唯物与唯心的分类表上却没有它们的格子。
hooks.text_en: **A third kind of real, neither matter nor mind**: money, Monday, companies, marriage, national borders. None of them grows in atoms or in any single person's thoughts; they persist because many people recognise them together, and would genuinely vanish if everyone stopped at once. Which column do they belong in? They shape ordinary lives more than almost anything else, and the materialist-idealist table has no cell for them.

hooks.text: **解释为什么让人觉得东西变假了**：告诉一个人他的爱情是催产素、他的敬畏是颞叶放电，很多人立刻觉得被贬低了；可没有人在知道彩虹是折射之后就不再看彩虹。这种「一被解释就掉价」的感觉从哪里来，它在什么时候是错的、又在什么时候其实提醒了我们什么？
hooks.text_en: **Why explanation can make a thing feel counterfeit**: tell someone their love is oxytocin and their awe is temporal-lobe activity and many will feel demoted on the spot — yet nobody stopped looking at rainbows on learning about refraction. Where does the sense of devaluation-by-explanation come from, when is it simply mistaken, and when is it warning us about something real?

hooks.text: **形而上学的政治史**：唯物与唯心不只是课堂上的两个选项，它们做过定罪的标签，也做过替现实开脱的说辞——贫穷被说成心相不正，苦难被说成历史必然。一套关于世界本原的主张，是怎样一步步变成关于人该忍受什么的主张的？
hooks.text_en: **The political history of a metaphysics**: materialism and idealism have not only been two options on a syllabus. They have served as labels for conviction and as excuses for the way things are — poverty attributed to an impure mind, suffering to historical necessity. By what steps does a claim about the origin of the world turn into a claim about what people ought to endure?

hooks.text: **怎么分辨一个「意识/能量/量子」的说法值不值得当真**：这类说法在市面上有真有假，而普通人手里并没有物理学训练。有没有几句不需要专业知识、当场就能问出口的话，能把知识、哲学与生意分开？
hooks.text_en: **How to tell whether a claim about consciousness, energy or the quantum deserves to be taken seriously**: such claims come both genuine and counterfeit, and an ordinary person has no training in physics to sort them. Are there a few questions, needing no expertise and askable on the spot, that separate knowledge from philosophy from sales?

answer.lead: 不需要懂物理，五句话就够用。**关键不在于你能不能判断它对不对，而在于它肯不肯把自己置于可能出错的位置。**

answer.tail: 五问之外还有一条底线：**任何让你停掉正在起效的治疗的说法，无论听起来多深奥，都先当它是错的。**说法可以慢慢辨，身体不能等。

answer_en.lead: No physics required; five sentences will do. **The point is not whether you can judge the claim correct, but whether it is willing to put itself anywhere it could be shown wrong.**

answer_en.tail: Beyond the five there is a floor: **any claim that asks you to stop a treatment that is working should be treated as false first, however deep it sounds.** Claims can be sorted out slowly; a body cannot wait.
